Life happens: people get busy, move, have strained relationships, or simply miss casual reminders. *If you didn't actively tell them*, you didn't extend a real invitation—you just assumed. - Example: If your boss said "all team members are welcome at the office party," but never shared the date/location, would you blame someone for not showing up? This isn't a private family moment—it's a public announcement that *your family gathered without her*. That’s why she felt "purposely excluded." If you’d genuinely wanted her there, you’d have ensured she knew about it *before* posting. 3. **"I didn’t get an invite and showed up" doesn’t fix this.** - Your own attendance proves you knew about the event through *other channels* (e.g., a group text, in-person talk). But if the sister-in-law wasn’t in those channels? That’s on you. If you’re the one organizing or celebrating the event, *you* bear responsibility for inclusive communication—not "they should’ve known." ### Why It’s Not Your Mother-in-Law’s Fault: - You said *you* posted the photo and *you* said "I didn’t get an invite and I showed up." That makes **you the de facto organizer** of this year’s event. Even if your mother-in-law pays, *you’re the one making it visible to the world*. If you’re going to publicize it, you must ensure everyone who should be there knows. ### How to Fix This: - **Apologize directly to your sister-in-law.** Say: *"I’m so sorry you didn’t know about the event. I should’ve made sure to reach out to you—my mistake. I’d love to have you join us next year, and I’ll personally make sure you’re included."* - **Next year:** Text/call everyone *by name* with clear details (date, time, place). Don’t rely on "everyone knows." - **Never post a family photo without checking**—especially if someone’s missing. It’s not "just a photo"; it’s a public signal of inclusion/exclusion. **Real community isn’t about assumptions—it’s about active care.** If you didn’t tell her, you excluded her. That’s not "not your fault"—it’s your responsibility. *(Note: In AITA terms, <1> = "You're the asshole.")*
